newsitem.title: GERMANY: BME/Reuters German PMI index shows faster growth.
newsitem.headline: BME/Reuters German PMI index shows faster growth.

text.p: Germany's manufacturing sector expanded at an accelerated pace in May although growing bottlenecks drove up prices, according to the BME/Reuters German Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI).

The index, first published last month and available exclusively through Reuters, rose to a seasonally-adjusted 57.49 in May from 56.58 in April, research group NTC Publications Ltd said in a statement.

It was the ninth consecutive monthly rise recorded in the seasonally-adjusted index since the survey began in April last year. NTC also said that for the first time since April 1996, companies did not report an overall decline in employment.
"Output, orders, purchasing and employment indexes all reached new highs," the statement said.
The index is based on a survey of 350 companies carried out by NTC in cooperation with the BME German Association for Materials Management, Purchasing and Logistics.

A reading below 50 percent indicates that the manufacturing economy is generally declining, while a level above 50 percent shows it generally expanding. The more it deviates from 50, the greater the improvement or decline in the current month.
NTC said rising demand for goods was putting pressure on suppliers whose lack of production capacity led to a rise in the number of purchasing managers reporting supply bottlenecks.
"The growing emergence of bottlenecks was often associated with rising prices charged by suppliers," NTC said.

Those price rises, coupled with the higher cost of imported materials arising from the continued weakness of the mark, led to the fourth consecutive monthly rise in the average price paid for inputs by panel members.
The price index component of the PMI rose to a seasonally-adjusted 55.98 in May from 55.04 in April.
